note: Ru2TaAl has been synthesized as a Heusler-type (L21) compound. Tseng et al. (Phys. Rev. B 96, 125106, 2017) measured resistivity, Seebeck, thermal conductivity, low-temperature specific heat and 27Al NMR. They report semiconductor-like resistivity and a residual Fermi-level density of states in the specific heat (semimetal with pseudogap), and no superconductivity is mentioned in the abstract. I could only read the abstract (paper is not open access), so the lowest temperature reached is not confirmed; it is a low-temperature specific-heat study, probably near 2 K, but this is unverified. An earlier report (Feng, Nandy, Pollock, Scripta Mater. 50, 849, 2004, DOI 10.1016/j.scriptamat.2003.12.013) found an L21 Ru2AlTa Heusler phase as a precipitate in a Ru-bearing Ni superalloy (structure/composition only, no low-temperature data). Relatives: Ru2NbAl (Heusler, semimetal, short-range ferromagnetic clusters below 5 K, no superconductivity reported; PRB 98, 205130, 2018); Ru2NbGa (semimetal, PRB 94, 205116, 2016); Ru2VAl (pseudogap thermoelectric); RuAl2 (semimetal). No superconductor found among these Ru2-X-Al/Ga Heuslers. Superconducting Ta-Ru phases of other structure: TaRuSi (Tc 3.9 K), TaRuB (Tc ~4 K); Heusler superconductor ScAu2Al (Tc ~5 K) is a different chemistry.

V2GaN has been synthesized as a 211 MAX phase (Kubitza et al., Inorg. Chem. 2022, 61, 10634), together with V2GaC and the carbonitride V2GaC1-xNx, characterized by XRD, electron microscopy and electron/X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A 2026 J. Adv. Ceram. paper (10.26599/jac.2026.9221382) made V2GaC1-xNx up to x=1 and measured only microwave absorption at room temperature. No low-temperature transport, magnetic or specific-heat data for V2GaN were found, and no superconductivity report; first-principles papers on M2GaN exist but are theory only. Relatives: V2GaC (made; no superconducting Tc confirmed in this search); V2GeN (made, 10.1021/acs.chemmater.3c02510): magnetic and transport data show an antiferromagnetic-paramagnetic-like transition at 160-200 K, no superconductivity reported in the abstract; V2GaC1-xNx carbonitrides (made). Mo2GaC is described as superconducting in a theory paper title (Physica C 2010) but no Tc was verified here.

Ru2VGa was first synthesized in 2013 (Mondal, Mazumdar, Ranganathan): Heusler Fm-3m, a = 5.994 A, with XRD from 12 K to 300 K showing no structural transition and resistivity that is high with a low residual resistivity ratio. A 2023 Intermetallics paper reports magnetic, transport, specific-heat and Seebeck data on Ru2VAl and Ru2VGa, describing them as metallic and disordered, with no superconductivity mentioned in the indexed title or keywords. I could not read the abstract or full text, so the lowest measurement temperature (probably about 2 K) is unconfirmed and the absence of a superconducting transition rests on no report of one in any record found. Other papers on Ru2VGa are theory (J. Alloys Compd. 2015, Ru2VGa1-xAlx), thermoelectrics of Ru2VAl1-xGax (Intermetallics 2018) and a 2026 hydrogen-evolution catalysis paper; none reports superconductivity. Relatives: Made: Ru2VAl (same 2013 and 2023 papers, no superconductivity reported), Ru2VAl1-xGax (thermoelectric alloys, 10.1016/j.intermet.2017.09.012), Ru2NbAl (short-range ferromagnetic clusters below 5 K, no superconductivity), Ru2CrGe/Ru2CrSn (antiferromagnet and spin glass). Heusler superconductors elsewhere: ZrNi2Ga (Tc 2.9 K, 10.1103/physrevb.78.184506). No superconducting Ru2VZ compound found.

Gauzzi et al. (Phys. Rev. B 66, 085106, 2002) synthesized AuVS2 single crystals (BaVS3 + Au, 700 C, 3 GPa) with hexagonal P63/mmc, a=3.224 A, c=15.039 A. In-plane ac resistivity was measured from room temperature down to 4.2 K: weakly insulating below ~250 K, resistivity stays below ~800 microohm cm at 4.2 K, with no superconductivity mentioned in the abstract; band structure gives a semimetal with near-zero DOS at E_F. Lowest temperature reached is 4.2 K (from abstract only; full text not read, closed access), so superconductivity below 4.2 K is not excluded. No specific-heat or magnetic data found. Relatives: V1/4VS2 (self-intercalated VS2) is superconducting only under high pressure (PRL 2026, not ambient); Ba_xV6S8 superconducts at ~2.5 K (Chem. Mater. 2001); bulk VS2 itself is hard to prepare stoichiometrically. No ambient-pressure superconducting Au-V-S phase found.

No paper found reporting synthesis of 1:1:1 LiGaIr (any element order, hexagonal P63/mmc or otherwise); only Materials Project computed entries (Li2GaIr, LiGaIr2) turned up for the Li-Ga-Ir system. The only experimentally known Li-Ga-Ir ternary found is the Heusler LiGa2Ir (Gornicka et al. 2021), which is bulk superconducting at Tc = 2.94 K; this is a different stoichiometry and structure, so it does not count as LiGaIr. Related REIrGa (RE = Sm, Lu) are made in TiNiSi type (Eustermann 2018) with no low-temperature data seen. Searches were by title/abstract only; no full texts were opened, and the Li-Ga-Ir phase diagram has not been seen in a dedicated report. Relatives: LiGa2Ir (Heusler Fm-3m, a=6.032 A), made, bulk superconductor Tc = 2.94 K, doi 10.1038/s41598-021-95944-1 (verified); LiGa2Rh isoelectronic Heusler superconductor (mentioned in that abstract, not independently checked); SmIrGa and LuIrGa (TiNiSi type), made, doi 10.1002/zaac.201800287 (verified), no Tc reported; IrGa2 and Ga3Ir binaries made (no superconductivity checked).

Muts, Poettgen and Zaremba (Z. Anorg. Allg. Chem. 633, 2591, 2007) synthesised SrAuIn3 from the elements in sealed Ta ampoules and solved it by single-crystal X-ray diffraction as BaNiSn3 type, I4mm, a = 456.97 pm, c = 1243.7 pm, with a small degree of Au/In disorder. Only structure and bonding are reported in the abstract. No resistivity, susceptibility or specific-heat data and no superconductivity report were found in about 7 searches across FastTrack, OpenAlex and Consensus (Consensus hit its usage limit). Only the abstract was read, not the full text, which is paywalled. Relatives: SrAuSi3 (BaNiSn3 type, made by high-pressure synthesis) is a bulk noncentrosymmetric superconductor, Tc about 1.5 to 1.6 K (10.1021/cm500032u; 10.1103/physrevb.93.054519). SrAuIn (TiNiSi type) and Sr5Au13.5In8.5 have also been made (structure only; 10.1515/znb-2011-1104). No superconducting AEAuIn3 relative was found.

No paper found reporting SrAgAl3 / SrAl3Ag (any element order) as synthesized, in the BaNiSn3-type or any other structure, and none reporting low-temperature measurements or superconductivity for it. The BaNiSn3 type is well known for LnTX3 compounds (e.g. LnAuAl3, CeCuAl3, LaIrSi3), and Hulliger (1995) reviews LnAuAl3 relatives, but I found no alkaline-earth-Ag-Al example. Searches were limited to titles/abstracts (Consensus was out of quota, OpenAlex keyword hits were irrelevant), so an unindexed ternary-phase-diagram or crystallographic-database entry cannot be ruled out. Relatives: Made BaNiSn3-type relatives: LnAuAl3 (Hulliger 1995, doi 10.1016/0925-8388(94)01389-6), CeCuAl3 and CeAuAl3, LaCuAl3 (all non-superconducting Ce/La aluminides in the lit. seen), BaAuxSn4-x (BaNiSn3 phase, doi 10.1021/ic402991d, not checked for Tc). Superconducting BaNiSn3-type: LaIrSi3, LaPdSi3, LaPtSi3 (silicides, not Sr/Al/Ag; Tc not verified here). Binary Sr-Al phases are SrAl2 and SrAl4 (BaAl4-type; Bruzzone and Merlo 1975, doi 10.1016/0022-5088(75)90212-x); SrAl4-xSix superconducts at 2.1 K (x=1.5) and 2.6 K (x=2) under high-pressure synthesis (doi 10.1021/acs.chemmater.6b04615). Binary SrAg exists (Merlo and Fornasini 1981).

CaPt2Ge2 was reported as made by Venturini, Malaman and Roques (J. Less-Common Met. 146, 271, 1989, doi 10.1016/0022-5088(89)90385-8; the ChemInform abstract lists MPt2Ge2 with M = Ca, Y, La-Dy, annealed at 1273 K), as a monoclinic variant of the tetragonal CaBe2Ge2 type. A 2013 NTHU thesis (doi 10.6843/nthu.2013.00560, in Chinese; Crossref does not register this DOI, so it was read from the OpenAlex abstract only) states that no Tc above 2 K was observed for monoclinic (P21) CaPt2Ge2; the lowest temperature reached is therefore about 2 K, and the abstract does not say whether it was resistivity or susceptibility. The Materials Project entry for Ca(PtGe)2 on OSTI (doi 10.17188/1696292) is also monoclinic P21, so the tetragonal P4/nmm form named in the brief appears not to be the reported ground-state structure. I found no low-temperature data below 2 K and no report of a tetragonal CaPt2Ge2 sample. Relatives: Superconducting: CaIr2Ge2 (bct, Tc 5.4 K, NTHU thesis); CaPd2Ge2 (ThCr2Si2-type, Tc about 1.7-2.0 K; Anand et al., J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 2014); tetragonal LaPt2-xGe2+x (CaBe2Ge2-type, Tc 1.85-1.95 K for x = 0.15-0.2, Maeda et al., JPSJ 2013), whereas monoclinic LaPt2Ge2 has a Tc about four times lower. Not superconducting: Ca2PtGe3 (no Tc down to 0.4 K); CaPtGe2 (not superconducting above 1.3 K); Ca(Ir1-xPtx)2Ge2 for x above 0.5 (Tc below 2 K). Also made: YPt2Ge2 (CaBe2Ge2-type, primitive tetragonal), CePt2Ge2 (antiferromagnet, TN 2.2 K), EuPt2Ge2, GdPt2Ge2.

No report of synthesis of PtPbTe was found under any element ordering (PtPbTe, PbPtTe, PtTePb, Pt Pb Te) or in Pt-Pb-Te phase-relation or mineral searches. The only hit for the formula string is a 2026 computational paper on hydrogen-evolution catalysts in chiral topological semimetals (10.1038/s42004-026-01985-w); its abstract suggests a high-throughput database screen, so it is not evidence of synthesis (full text not read). The analogous Pt-Bi-Te system (2026 phase-equilibria study, 10.1180/mgm.2026.10196) reports the maslovite analogue PtBiTe could not be obtained at 350-550 C, and PtSnTe is reported in a pyrite-related ordered structure rather than ullmannite-type. Lead is very large and Pb-Pt-Te intermetallic chemistry looks unfavourable, so this may be a hypothetical compound. Relatives: PtSbS (ullmannite-type, P2_13, made, bulk superconductor Tc = 0.15 K, 10.7566/jpsj.88.093709); PtSnS/PtSnSe/PtSnTe (made, pyrite-related ordered semiconductors, no superconductivity reported, 10.1016/j.jssc.2004.03.031); PtBiTe (maslovite, mineral; synthetic ternary not obtained in 10.1180/mgm.2026.10196); PtTe2 (binary, no Pb) and PdTe2 (superconductor, ~1.6 K, 10.1103/physrevlett.120.156401).

Hlukhyy, Eck and Fassler (Inorg. Chem. 45, 7408, 2006) report SrNiSn2 as a new compound made by arc melting and annealing at 1270 K, with single-crystal X-ray structure in CeNiSi2 type (Cmcm, a=4.5924, b=18.710, c=4.5228 A). The paper covers bonding and ELF electronic-structure analysis; the abstract mentions no transport, magnetic or specific-heat measurements. A German-language companion (Z. Anorg. Allg. Chem. 2006, 10.1002/zaac.200670172) and a ChemInform abstract cover the same work. No paper found reporting low-temperature data or superconductivity for SrNiSn2, though searches were limited to abstracts/titles. Relatives: CaNiGe2 and SrNiGe2 (same CeNiSi2 type, same paper); no superconducting relative found in these searches.
